patterns_data.top_pattern: IN DSNP HMO spend is trapped in a massive Not Mapped bucket
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: IN DSNP HMO / Not Mapped facility bucket
patterns_data.pattern_details: IN DSNP HMO spend is heavily concentrated in a Not Mapped facility bucket, adding about $66.0M. Claim volume also increased materially, but because the facility classification is missing, it is not possible to tell whether the change reflects true utilization growth, a site-of-care shift, or a mapping problem. This should be treated as a gating validation issue before broader authorization, reimbursement, or network actions are taken in IN DSNP HMO.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A misclassified bucket this large can distort every downstream conclusion about provider mix, site of care, and utilization management performance.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Validate and reclassify the IN DSNP HMO Not Mapped claims at the facility and product level, then rerun authorization, reimbursement, and provider analyses only after the mapping issue is resolved.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase sits in a Not Mapped facility bucket and is explicitly flagged as unmapped or unknown, so business action should wait for classification cleanup.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO in the Not Mapped facility bucket added about +$66.0M.
Claim count increased by 123,376, with unit cost indicators also moving up.
This single bucket represents about 80% of the positive delta in its evidence set.
The contributing group carries an unmapped or unknown value flag.

patterns_data.top_pattern: UNATTRIBUTED outpatient temporary-code spend needs validation before action
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: UNATTRIBUTED outpatient ancillary and management categories
patterns_data.pattern_details: UNATTRIBUTED outpatient spend rose sharply in OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc, concentrated in Not Mapped claims tied to diagnosis R69 and temporary code groupings. patterns_data.why_it_matters: Unattributed temporary-code spend of this size can misdirect both utilization management and payment policy if it is treated as normal clinical growth.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a targeted data-quality and coding review on the UNATTRIBUTED OP HH/DME and OP Mgmt Oth Misc claims, focusing on R69 and temporary code buckets, then route only validated findings to clinical and UM teams.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in UNATTRIBUTED, Not Mapped, and temporary-code claims with repeated unmapped signals, so attribution and classification must be confirmed first.

UNATTRIBUTED OP Mgmt Oth Misc added about +$22.6M on 63,836 more claims across temporary code buckets.

patterns_data.top_pattern: IN DSNP HMO home health is showing real volume and cost pressure
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: IN DSNP HMO / HOME HEALTH - FREESTANDING
patterns_data.pattern_details: IN DSNP HMO home health at freestanding providers added about $7.1M and appears to reflect both more utilization and higher payment intensity. The business lever is home health authorization discipline, visit management, and contract review.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Home health growth can scale quickly in DSNP populations if visit controls and reimbursement terms are not aligned.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Launch an IN DSNP HMO home health action plan that audits top episodes and visit patterns, tightens prior authorization and continued-stay criteria, and checks paid rates against contract terms for freestanding home health.
evidence_summary: IN DSNP HMO home health added about +$7.1M.

patterns_data.pattern_details: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend is being pushed by a small set of very high-cost IP Med/Surg cases rather than broad-based utilization growth. The pattern centers on pancreatic disorders, pulmonary embolism, complex lower-extremity procedures, and inflammatory bowel disease, with several single-case increases near $0.2M. Some of the clinical records also show null or blank procedure fields, so case review and data validation should occur together.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Rare inpatient outliers need case-level intervention because the right lever may be catastrophic claim review, clinical management, payment integrity, or benefit design rather than broad utilization policy.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Open case-level review on the cited TX admissions, validate procedure completeness, and confirm whether outlier payment, case management, or acute inpatient authorization controls should be adjusted for these high-cost Med/Surg episodes.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The increase is concentrated in very small case counts and several clinical records contain null or blank procedure fields, so case details should be confirmed before policy action.
evidence_summary: TX IP Med/Surg rare-case groups total about +$1.9M when clinical and DSNP HMO acute hospital views are combined.
Key drivers include pulmonary embolism without MCC, pancreatic disorders with MCC, lower-extremity or humerus procedures with MCC, and inflammatory bowel disease with CC.
Several individual increases are about $0.2M on only 1 to 5 claims.

patterns_data.why_it_matters: Transportation spend can expand quickly through coding, routing, or authorization gaps, and a single-provider concentration makes this highly actionable.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Audit Midwest Medical Transport Company claims in OH for facility mapping, transport classification, and prior authorization or edit compliance, then decide whether the increase reflects valid transport utilization or preventable leakage.
patterns_data.validation_reason: All contributing groups are tied to Not Mapped or unmapped-value signals, and the pattern is concentrated at one transportation provider across products.
evidence_summary: OH not-mapped transportation-related claims total about +$576K across Medicare HMO and DSNP HMO.
